newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Danu could take over Finance One-paper.
newsitem.headline: Thai Danu could take over Finance One-paper.

text.p: The merger between Thai Danu Bank Plc and Finance One Plc could be changed into a takeover deal by the bank instead of a merger, local newspapers reported on Friday.

The Bangkok Post quoted Thirachai Phuvanatnaranubala, the director of the Financial Institutions Supervision and Development Department, as saying the government would give its full support to a takeover.

Thirachai said a merger was not feasible, adding that the central bank was seeking a new approach that would allow the new firm sufficient qualifications to get a banking licence, the Bangkok Post said.

The comments come amid rumours that the biggest merger among Thai financial institutions was said to be in danger of collapsing because Thai Danu was planning to walk away from the deal due to various problems.
A Thai Danu official told a news conference on Wednesday that the merger with Thailand's largest finance company, Finance One, was still on and the boards were due to approve it on May 15.

"The boards of Finance One and Thai Danu are scheduled to hold meetings on May 15 to approve the merger after the due diligence is completed," Chaiwat Utaiwan, executive vice president of Thai Danu, said on Wednesday.
But The Nation newspaper said Thirachai said the central bank hoped if Thai Danu would take over Finance One it could speed up the rescue of the finance company.
Rumours still abound that due diligence will expose Finance One's weak financial position and the company's shareholders may not approve the merger.
Analysts say Finance One sought the merger because it faced liquidity problems which emerged amid a major shakeup of Thailand's troubled finance sector.
